two_further_structural_confirmations.READOUT_at_the_last_layer: restoration exactly 1.000000 with a zero-width interval, as it must be: patching the final position's final-block state installs the donor's answer state verbatim
two_further_structural_confirmations.CUE_at_layer_5: 1.019956, consistent with a full conversion of the run

gate_2_prefix_integrity.diagnosis: the offset is in the baseline, not in the patch

the_observation_that_settles_it.statement: PREFIX at layer 27 is a no-op guaranteed by the architecture rather than merely by causal masking: the last block's output at a non-final position is read by NOTHING, because only the final position reaches the unembedding. It would read zero even if the patched values were arbitrary.
the_observation_that_settles_it.therefore: a patch that provably cannot influence the output still moves the metric, so patching is not the source

gate_2_prefix_integrity.the_actual_cause: the clean baseline LD is measured in a batch-of-one forward while every patched LD is measured in a batch-of-48 forward; bfloat16 kernels do not select the same reduction order at both batch sizes, so a constant per-unit offset enters every restoration value
gate_2_prefix_integrity.who_is_at_fault: the implementation, not the registration; the registered tolerance was right to refuse it
gate_2_prefix_integrity.the_fix_not_applied_here: include an explicit self-patch job in the same batch and use it as the baseline. That is an implementation change in the direction the precedent permits, but it requires re-running the measurement, and the registration says to stop and report rather than self-repair
gate_2_prefix_integrity.estimated_cost_of_the_rerun: about 0.11 actively used GPU-hours, the same as the run just performed

the_second_problem_which_is_heavier.id: the estimand does not separate two different movements
the_second_problem_which_is_heavier.statement: restoration is normalised on LD = logit(donor target) - logit(recipient target). Any patch that merely DISRUPTS the recipient's own answer lowers logit(recipient target) and therefore raises restoration, without carrying one bit of information about the donor. The registered estimand cannot tell 'moved toward the donor's answer' apart from 'moved away from the recipient's answer'.

the_evidence_that_this_is_not_hypothetic.reading: the null constructions are not quiet. A patch carrying no donor information at all produces movement of the same order as the real patch, which is exactly what the disruption pathway predicts

the_second_problem_which_is_heavier.why_this_is_the_EQ2_lesson_recurring: EQ2 recorded that a null carrying a small real signal produced a band under a rule that assumed the null was empty. Here the nulls were built correctly and the ceiling absorbed the disruption, so the rule did NOT manufacture a positive and the conservative direction held. But the same underlying error is present one level down, in the estimand rather than in the null
the_second_problem_which_is_heavier.consequence: the measurement is conservative and underpowered rather than wrong. As specified it cannot distinguish a carried intermediate from generic disruption at the same site

the_ceiling_scale_problem.registered_rule: one scalar maximum over every null construction, replicate, site other than PREFIX, and layer
the_ceiling_scale_problem.why_it_happens: a norm-matched random vector at the READOUT position destroys the state the answer is read from, and the normalised restoration of a destroyed run is unbounded; the same construction at BRIDGE perturbs a position the answer is not read from. One scalar maximum therefore imports the READOUT scale into a BRIDGE test
the_ceiling_scale_problem.why_the_OD_011_demonstration_did_not_cat: the demonstration used synthetic nulls at sigma 0.05 and 0.15, the scale of an in-distribution null. It proved the rule cannot manufacture a positive from a quiet null, and that remains true. It did not prove the ceiling is on the right scale, and I did not think to require that it should
the_ceiling_scale_problem.not_repaired_here_because: the BRIDGE curve is already in hand, so choosing a per-site ceiling now would move the registered text toward the data. The directionality precedent calls that p-hacking regardless of whether the replacement rule is better in the abstract
